- (F) finiteness / large-prime erasure lemma: membership depends only on primes in a finite set, because any term divisible by a large prime is dominated by a smaller number with the same small-prime support that is itself a term — proved for ALL terms.
- (P) periodicity assembly: with L = product of finitely many relevant primes, membership invariant under m -> m+L for every m >= a_1 (from the first term), T = number of terms in a window of length L, giving a_{n+T} = a_n + L for all n >= 1.

Actually the standard counterexample: a_n could be divisible by extra primes because the number with minimal prime support may be too small (less than a_n). E.g., P(a_{n+1}) need not be minimal since a_{n+1} just needs to be > a_n and hit all previous supports; the smallest such number could have prime support containing extra primes because smaller numbers with minimal supports are below a_n. Indeed in the example computed in the write-up itself: a_2 = 18 = {2,3} — hitting set for {{3,5}} needs to contain 3 or 5. {2,3} is not a minimal hitting set? Minimal hitting sets for {{3,5}} are {3} and {5}. {2,3} contains {3} as a proper subset. So P(a_2) = {2,3} is NOT a minimal hitting set for F_1.
